name: Experimental evidence of neutrinos produced in the CNO fusion cycle in the Sun
title: Experimental evidence of neutrinos produced in the CNO fusion cycle in the Sun

claim.quote: Experimental evidence of neutrinos produced in the CNO fusion cycle in the Sun

summary.plain: Borexino found, for the first time, the faint signal of neutrinos from the Sun's secondary fusion cycle (the CNO cycle) — the process that dominates in heavier stars.
summary.technical: Direct observation, with high statistical significance, of CNO-cycle solar neutrinos, identified as an excess of a few counts per day per 100 t of target above backgrounds in the Borexino liquid-scintillator detector at LNGS — the first experimental evidence of this process.

why_it_matters.value: First experimental confirmation that the CNO fusion cycle, thought to dominate energy production in stars more massive than the Sun, actually occurs in stellar cores; also informs the solar metallicity problem.
why_it_matters.quote: This is the first experimental evidence of this process obtained with the unprecedentedly radio-pure large-volume liquid-scintillator Borexino detector

key_value_text.value: Excess of a few counts per day per 100 t of target attributed to CNO-neutrino interactions
key_value_text.quote: the excess of the few counts per day per 100 tonnes of target due to CNO neutrino interactions above the backgrounds

significance.value: high statistical significance (exact sigma not stated in the fetched abstract)
significance.quote: the direct observation, with a high statistical significance, of neutrinos produced in the CNO cycle in the Sun
significance.note: The abstract fetched this session states 'high statistical significance' but not a numeric sigma value.
